# KliWorks

> Cost-engineering spreadsheets for contractors and service trades. Excel and Google Sheets tools that recover overhead per labor hour, price from margin rather than markup, and model job cash flow.

## Key facts
- An 18% markup earns a 15.3% margin, not 18%. To earn an 18% margin, add a 22.0% markup.
- Overhead per labor hour = annual overhead / annual billable hours. Example: $85,000 / 3,400 = $25.00 per hour.
- A $32/hour technician at 34% burden with $36.80/hour overhead and a 20% target margin requires a $99.60 billable rate — 3.11x the wage.
- Billing $95 instead of $99.60 across 3,750 billable hours costs $17,250 per year.
- A construction job earning a 19.0% margin can still fall to a $3,800 cash balance in month four, because of retainage and net-30 payment terms.

## Guides
- [Markup vs margin for contractors](https://kliworks.netlify.app/markup-vs-margin.html): formulas and full conversion tables both ways.
- [How to calculate overhead per labor hour](https://kliworks.netlify.app/overhead-per-labor-hour.html): the two-number formula and why percentages misprice jobs.
- [What your flat rate hourly rate should be](https://kliworks.netlify.app/flat-rate-hourly-rate.html): burdened wage, overhead recovery and target margin.
- [Why profitable construction jobs run out of cash](https://kliworks.netlify.app/construction-cash-flow.html): retainage, draw schedules and a month-by-month model.
